2027-03-08.title: Fifth Monday of the Great Fast
2027-03-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Sell all and give to the poor
2027-03-08.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). The Latin Church commemorates St John of God today.
2027-03-08.verse: There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.
theo: The fifth week of the Great Fast opens with a warning that sounds, at first, almost against fasting. Some teachers in Colossae had turned religion into a matter of diet and calendar, of visions and the worship of angels, and they judged the believers who did not keep their rules. Paul writes: “Therefore do not let anyone condemn you in matters of food and drink or of observing festivals, new moons, or sabbaths. These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.” Paul does not despise fasting; the Church fasted from the beginning, and the St Thomas Christians have kept the fifty days of the Great Fast with great seriousness for centuries, giving up meat and fish, often eating one meal a day, sometimes sleeping on a mat on the floor. But every practice is a shadow, and a shadow is cast by something solid. The solid thing is Christ. A fast that makes me proud, or that makes me watch what my neighbour eats, has kept the shadow and lost the substance. Paul names the root of the trouble: such people are “not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, nourished and held together by its ligaments and sinews, grows with a growth that is from God.” The Great Fast is meant to bind us more closely to the Head and to one another, never to divide the body into the strict and the lax.

In the Gospel a ruler comes to Jesus with the deepest question a person can ask: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” Jesus points him to the commandments, and the man answers honestly: “I have kept all these since my youth.” He is no hypocrite. He has kept the law, the shadow, faithfully. Then Jesus looks at him and says: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” The one thing lacking is not one more rule. It is a Person: come, follow me. “But when he heard this, he became sad; for he was very rich.” Jesus does not run after him to lower the price. He says, with sorrow: “How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!” Not everyone is called to sell everything, as the apostles and the religious do; but everyone is asked what holds the heart. The Latin Church today remembers St John of God, a Portuguese soldier and bookseller who, after hearing a sermon in Granada, gave away his stock of books and spent the rest of his life carrying the sick poor into a house he opened for them. In many of our parishes the money saved by fasting is put into a Lenten box for the poor. It is a small way of hearing the same word: sell, give, come, follow.
outline: Ask: what is the one thing still lacking in me?
Fasting points to Christ and must never divide the body.
A good man who stopped one step short.
Treasure in heaven and the eye of the needle.
live: Put into your parish's Lenten box, or give directly to someone in need, what your fasting has saved this week.
Today, say nothing about what others eat or do not eat, and let your own fast be known only to God.
2027-03-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the substance of every shadow and the treasure of every heart. Do not let our fasting make us proud or quick to judge, but bind us more closely to you, our Head, and to one another. Show us the one thing still lacking in us, and give us the courage not to go away sad, but to give, and to come, and to follow you. Through the prayers of St John of God, make us servants of the sick and the poor. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the shadow gives way to the substance: the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ, and the Head nourishes the whole body that grows with a growth that is from God.

quick: Paul: food rules and feast days are a shadow; the substance belongs to Christ.
The rich ruler kept every commandment but would not follow when Jesus called.
The one thing lacking is not another rule but a Person: come, follow me.
2027-03-08.action: Give to the poor today what your fasting has saved.
2027-03-08.question: What is the one thing still lacking in my following of Christ?

family.explain: A rich young man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. He had kept all of God's rules. Jesus loved him and said: give your things to the poor and come with me. But the man loved his things too much, and he went away sad. Jesus wants to be more important to us than anything we own.
family.intention: We pray for the sick in hospitals, and for all who care for them, through the prayers of St John of God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there one thing we own that we could share with someone who needs it this week?”

illus: A retired teacher in Pala kept the Great Fast strictly for fifty years: no meat, no fish, one meal a day. She also kept a careful eye on her daughters-in-law, and could tell you who in the parish had eaten fish on a Friday. One Lenten evening her small granddaughter, filling the family's Lenten box for the poor with coins, asked her: Ammachi, who are we fasting for? The old woman began to answer, stopped, and said nothing for a long time. That year, the family remembers, she stopped counting other people's plates and began cooking for a sick neighbour instead.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the substance of all we hope for. Come and hold us together as your body. Amen.
share: The substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:17). Where has my religious practice become a shadow without substance?
There is still one thing lacking (Luke 18:22). What is the one thing the Lord is asking me to let go?
He became sad; for he was very rich (Luke 18:23). What riches, of money, comfort or reputation, make me sad when Jesus calls?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich in you.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may always lead to Christ and to charity.
For the sick and for all who serve in hospitals, through the prayers of St John of God.
For the poor who will receive the alms of our Lenten boxes.
For those who are rich, that they may be generous and free.
For our group, that we may follow when Jesus calls.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Son, the treasure hidden in the field. Free our hearts from every lesser treasure, so that we may sell, give, and follow him with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul warns the Colossians: do not let anyone condemn you in matters of food and drink or of festivals; these are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:16–17).

We fast seriously in this Great Fast, as our forefathers did. But the fast is a shadow cast by Christ. If it makes us proud, or makes us judge our neighbour's plate, we have kept the shadow and lost the substance. Let our fast bind us to Christ, our Head, and to one another.

A rich ruler had kept all the commandments since his youth. Jesus told him: there is still one thing lacking; sell all that you own, give to the poor, and come, follow me (Luke 18:22). The man went away sad, for he was very rich.

The one thing lacking is not another rule; it is Jesus himself. St John of God gave away his books and spent his life carrying the sick poor. What holds my heart? This week let us give what our fast has saved, and follow him more closely. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus said: share what you have with the poor and come with me. But he loved his things too much and went away sad. Can you share one of your things with someone this week, and stay close to Jesus?

intro: Theme: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”
The shadow and the substance, the good man who stopped one step short, and the call to follow Jesus with an undivided heart.

q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?
These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
points.apply: Let your fast today end in one act of justice or kindness to someone who is burdened.

sub: A good man with a sincere question.
A Person, not one more rule.
q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.
points.apply: Ask the Lord in silence today: what is the one thing still lacking in me? Write down the answer.

q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Give this week, to the Lenten box or to a person in need, what your fasting has saved.

concl: Every fast is a shadow; Christ is the substance, and he asks for the heart, not only the plate.
The ruler kept the commandments and went away sad; let us give, and come, and follow.
2027-03-08.resolve: Give away this week what the fast has saved, and do not judge anyone else's fast.
